However, despite the crowd, the orders came surprisingly fast as usual, and there was no noticeable delay in serving the food. The overall ambience was lively and comfortable for a casual dinner.

We ordered Mushroom with White Pesto Sauce Pizza, Spinach & Corn Sandwich, Chicken Burger, Chocolate Croissant, Potato Wedges, and Blueberry Cheesecake.

🍕 Mushroom with White Pesto Sauce Pizza
This was one of the highlights of our meal. The pizza was fresh, flavorful, and delicious. The mushroom and white pesto sauce combination worked really well, and the pizza had a nice overall balance of flavors. Definitely something I would consider ordering again.

🥪 Spinach & Corn Sandwich
The sandwich was good in terms of taste and came in a generous portion. In fact, the quantity is easily enough for two people. For one person, finishing the entire sandwich might be a little difficult unless you have a big appetite. A good option if you're sharing.

🍔 Chicken Burger – Disappointing
Unfortunately, this was the worst item of the meal for me. The chicken burger was very disappointing, especially compared with the other food we ordered. The taste simply didn't work for me, and I wouldn't recommend it based on my experience.

🥐 Chocolate Croissant – ⭐ Top Notch
The chocolate croissant was easily the standout item of the evening. It was crunchy on the outside, warm, and generously filled with chocolate. Having it hot made it even better. The combination of the crisp texture and warm chocolate filling was excellent. Definitely worth trying if you visit Glen's.

🥔 Potato Wedges
The potato wedges were decent and went well as a side dish. Nothing extraordinary, but they were satisfying alongside the main items.

🫐 Blueberry Cheesecake
The blueberry cheesecake was a pleasant way to finish the meal. It had a nice dessert-like sweetness and complemented the rest of the meal well.

⭐ Overall Experience

Overall, it was a mixed but enjoyable experience. The restaurant was busy during the night, but the quick service was impressive, with no significant waiting time for our orders.

The Mushroom White Pesto Pizza and Chocolate Croissant were the clear winners for me. The Spinach & Corn Sandwich was also good, particularly considering its generous portion. On the other hand, the Chicken Burger was a major disappointment and definitely not something I'd order again.

My picks: 🍕 Mushroom White Pesto Pizza | 🥐 Chocolate Croissant
Best for sharing: 🥪 Spinach & Corn Sandwich
Would skip: 🍔 Chicken Burger

Overall, worth a visit for the bakery items and pizza, especially if you're looking for a casual place with relatively quick service even when it's If you’re looking for a place that feels less like a commercial cafeteria and more like an authentic South Indian kitchen, this is it. The ambience is neat, clean, and has a very traditional, welcoming South Indian setup. It’s a great spot to bring family for a proper meal, or even just to hit up with friends when you’re genuinely craving some "homestyle" non-veg food.
The Specialty: Chettinad Flavors
Thenmanam is all about that intense, spicy, and aromatic Chettinad profile.
The Must-Try: Their Mutton Biryani is a fan favorite, known for using Seeraga Samba rice which gives it that classic, authentic local taste.
The "Nei Soru" Experience: If you want something truly comforting, go for the Nei Soru (Ghee Rice) paired with Eral (Prawn) Thokku. It’s the kind of meal that just warms you up.
The Sides: Their Chicken Chinthamani is a highlight—it’s got that perfect kick of dry red chilies and native spices. If you’re feeling adventurous, they have a solid range of traditional seafood and mutton starters that actually taste like they came straight out of a home kitchen.
Service & Value
The service is generally polite, though it can get pretty crowded during peak hours (especially on weekends), so be prepared for a short wait. It’s a mid-range restaurant, so it’s not exactly "cheap eats," but the quality of the masalas and the authentic preparation makes it worth the spend for a special meal.
The Verdict
Thenmanam is a solid addition to Chennai’s food scene for anyone who loves deep, punchy South Indian flavors. It’s not your typical "fast food" joint—it’s for when you want to sit down, slow down, and actually enjoy your food. I’ve tried most of the well-known Kerala restaurants like Ente Keralam, Mallu Joint, Kumarakom, etc. Before coming here, I honestly thought Kumarakom was the best. But after eating here, I can confidently say this place is the best of the best.

From pricing to ambience, everything is excellent. The staff are extremely friendly, and what really sets this place apart is authenticity — unlike most Kerala restaurants where the waiters are usually North Indian or local staff, here everyone from the waiter to the server is a Keralite, which truly gives you that real Kerala feel.

The prices are also the cheapest compared to other Kerala restaurants, without compromising on quality.

Coming to the food — no words, just come and try. I had four different dishes, and every single one of them was excellent.

The food quality here is the real star. The rice is beautifully fragrant, perfectly spiced, and served piping hot alongside rich tomato chutney and flavorful soup. We tried the Al Fahm Mandi and Mutton Mandi—the meat was tender, fall-off-the-bone juicy, and paired brilliantly with the rice. The portion sizes are generous, making it ideal for feasting with family or large groups of friends.
The ambiance is lively, featuring traditional majlis-style floor seating alongside regular tables. However, because of its immense popularity, peak hours (especially weekends) can see heavy rush and long waiting times, so better queue management at the entrance would be a welcome improvement.

The ambience was quite simple for a 5-star hotel, but the food more than made up for it. The buffet had a generous spread of starters, mains, and desserts, and almost everything we tried was absolutely delicious.

Among the salads, the apple and pear salad was especially refreshing and flavourful. The samosa chaat turned out to be another highlight of the buffet. I also loved the veg sushi, the two varieties of hummus, and the veg dim sums, which were perfectly done.

Moving on to the main course, all the curries suited my taste wonderfully. My favourites were the vegetable spheres in Manchurian sauce, double baked potato, and the comforting panch ratan dal. I also got to try foxnut (makhana) curry, which was quite unique. I usually skip noodles at buffets, but their crispy chilli garlic noodles were surprisingly good.

Desserts were delightful too. The sponge cake was the highlight, along with the motichoor cream cheese dessert. One particularly fun detail was the Women’s Day decorations placed on the desserts — small cards that looked like paper. When I tried to remove one from my plate, it melted between my fingers… and that’s when I realised it was actually chocolate, beautifully crafted to create the illusion of a decorative card!

The fried Bengali sweet wasn’t really to my liking, but everything else was truly enjoyable.

Women’s Day with a beautiful Sunday brunch at Six 'O' One, and it turned out to be a lovely experience.

The ambience was quite simple for a 5-star hotel, but the food more than made up for it. The buffet had a generous spread of starters, mains, and desserts, and almost everything we tried was absolutely delicious.

Among the salads, the apple and pear salad was especially refreshing and flavourful. The samosa chaat turned out to be another highlight of the buffet. I also loved the veg sushi, the two varieties of hummus, and the veg dim sums, which were perfectly done.

Moving on to the main course, all the curries suited my taste wonderfully. My favourites were the vegetable spheres in Manchurian sauce, double baked potato, and the comforting panch ratan dal. I also got to try foxnut (makhana) curry, which was quite unique. I usually skip noodles at buffets, but their crispy chilli garlic noodles were surprisingly good.

Desserts were delightful too. The sponge cake was the highlight, along with the motichoor cream cheese dessert. One particularly fun detail was the Women’s Day decorations placed on the desserts — small cards that looked like paper. When I tried to remove one from my plate, it melted between my fingers… and that’s when I realised it was actually chocolate, beautifully crafted to create the illusion of a decorative card!

The fried Bengali sweet wasn’t really to my liking, but everything else was truly enjoyable.

To top it all off, the live music during the brunch made the celebration feel even more special, adding a lovely vibe to the afternoon. 🎶

I booked the Premium Cabin package at Restaurant on de roof to celebrate birthday, expecting a premium experience. Instead, it was a total waste of money. The management completely failed to deliver on their promises, and the entire mood of the celebration was ruined.
Here is a detailed breakdown of everything that went wrong:
Ruined Welcome & Surprise-
We booked the 11:30 PM slot, arrived on time, and were made to wait in our car until 11:45 PM. When we finally went up, the staff set up the flower shower and sparkling candles right in front of the birthday boy, completely ruining the surprise. While the fireworks worked, the flower shower dropped only 3-4 petals. We had to request a redo, which was done without the firecrackers, resulting in awkward and underwhelming pictures. To make matters worse, the promised bouquet consisted of old, dead flowers wrapped untidily in an old, frayed ribbon with threads coming out.
Moreover the surprise pathway is in front of washroom which looks like public bus stand toilet.
Ignored Decor Requests & Shabby Cabin-
I specifically requested birthday decor, not a Valentine's theme. They ignored this completely, giving us a "Love" LED sign instead of "Happy Birthday" and heart decorations everywhere. The cabin felt incredibly shabby and used by a previous couple:
The balloons were deflated and tiny.
The artificial flowers on the heart arch were faded.
The background curtains were a mess (we had to arrange them ourselves for photos).
The carpet in the cabin was peeling and coming out.
Terrible Amenities & Broken Photo Frames-
They promised 10 photos of the birthday boy. The pictures provided were terrible quality, 2-3 were actually torn, and the wooden stand was broken so it kept falling over. The dinner table was so small that a cake barely fit and things were falling off. There was no dustbin, leaving us to throw tissues around until we explicitly asked for one. Additionally, the cabin fan wasn't working when we entered. We had to fix the switch ourselves just to get a tiny table fan running in a very hot rooftop setting.
Absent Service-
Though the staff was polite, they were completely engaged on the first floor. There was zero attendance on the second floor where the cabins are. Because it was a late-night slot, the staff seemed tired and just left us alone. We had to constantly walk to the desk to search for salt, tissues, and follow up on our food. It felt like a self-service restaurant.
Disappointing Food-
Cake: Promised a blueberry cake; received a basic, average-tasting vanilla cake with cheap blueberry icing.
Soups: The Lemon Coriander Chicken soup was just lemon water with coriander and 2 chicken pieces. The Cream of Tomato was essentially garlic tomato water in a bowl.
Starters: Our non-veg starter never arrived! When we asked about it during the main course, they casually informed us they forgot and made an excuse that they thought we ordered extra main course instead.
Mocktails: The Chili Guava and Pina Colada were absolutely awful.
I am attaching pictures of the deflated balloons, broken frame, dead flower bouquet, watery soup, and peeling carpet as proof. I strongly urge the management to take action and train their team to serve customers properly. Until then, I highly recommend going to a different restaurant to celebrate your special occasions.

The Only Positives-
To be fair, the staff was very polite when speaking to us. Also, since we were the last couple left at the end of the night, they kindly accepted our request to play Bollywood songs. However, these small gestures couldn't save the overall Add a turf right behind it and the place becomes a magnet for crowds, a steady river of people flowing in and out with the enthusiasm of students after a match.

Every person on the team carried a quiet efficiency that deserves genuine applause.

It was warm and comforting, its sweetness just right, although the texture leaned a little thin, as if holding back from achieving greatness out of shyness. Then came the peri peri french fries, crisp outside, soft inside, each bite almost singing. The mayo and ketchup were perfect companions, though the peri peri masala was enthusiastic enough to wake the dead and the fries could have used a touch more crispness.

The peri peri chicken followed and instantly stole the night. The outer layer had that satisfying crunch, the inside was tender to the point of being luxurious, and the dips, though excellent, felt unnecessary when the chicken stood so confidently on its own. And then arrived the churros, a masterpiece disguised as dessert. Crisp to the touch, fragile in the best way, melting the moment it entered the mouth. Paired with caramel and chocolate, the caramel took a narrow lead, though both were delightful.

In the end, it felt like a place where the heart of the café beat in its kitchen and its people. The ambience and décor may still be waiting for their moment of glory, but with food this good and service this attentive, one scarcely minds. It is a place I will return to without hesitation, hoping the name remains the only strange thing about it.

It sits right in the middle of a busy stretch, which gives it visibility but also gifts it its first great flaw: parking, or rather the complete absence of it. Stopping there feels less like arriving at a café and more like negotiating with traffic for temporary mercy. If you do find a spot on the road, you park with the guilt of someone committing a small civic crime.

The second challenge is the open air layout. In a city like Chennai, where humidity clings to you like a second shirt, this is less charming design choice and more endurance activity. Yes, there are little fans trying their best, but by the time you finish your coffee you are also finishing a respectable amount of perspiration. Then comes the outdoor seating near the pavement. Quite apart from the fact that it is an obvious encroachment, the real issue is that those tables were so poorly maintained and dirty that we avoided them altogether and chose the bar seats closer to the shop instead. A café this chic should not have seating that looks like it was forgotten by the management and remembered only by dust.

And yet, once those flaws are set aside, the place has real charm. The interiors are beautifully done. The wood panelling, the counter, the chalkboard menu, the lighting, the coffee setup, everything works together with unusual elegance. It is the kind of café where you can see the decorator’s fingerprints on every corner, and for that person alone, a round of applause is due.

The staff added to the good mood. They were warm, approachable, and genuinely helpful with suggestions, which made the whole experience feel more welcoming than many trendier places manage. We ordered the cold Coconut Coffee, and it turned out to be the true heart of the visit. It was creamy, balanced, and sweet without crossing into syrupy territory. The flavour was just right, comforting and polished. The only issue was the texture, which was not completely smooth and carried a slight coarseness that held it back from perfection.

Origins Coffee feels less like a place that failed and more like a place aspiring beautifully within its constraints. It has drawbacks that are impossible to ignore, but it also has enough taste, warmth, and promise to make you forgive more than you planned to.

It can get a little chaotic during rush hours, though.

KUP is especially known for its beverages — from cold brews and latte frappes to refreshing coolers. I’ve tried quite a few, and they’ve consistently impressed my taste buds.

We visited TikTalk Café for dinner.
I want to clearly mention that food taste was good for us and we have no complaints regarding the food.

However, there are serious issues that need immediate attention:

1. Bathroom Hygiene – Very Poor

- Washbasin tap water was continuously flowing and could not be stopped.
- Floors and washbasin were dirty and poorly maintained.
- The toilet seat and area were unhygienic, with a strong bad smell, giving a public-toilet-like experience.
- A sticker saying “Keep the toilet clean” is pasted, but basic cleanliness itself is not maintained.

"Cleanliness should start from management, not customers."

2. Overall Cleanliness

Tables were not cleaned properly after previous customers. For a café, this directly affects the dining experience and comfort.

3. Service Speed

Service was extremely slow, even though we visited during non-peak hours and we were the only customers seated at that time.

4. Staff Behavior

Staff members were polite, which is appreciated. But politeness alone is not enough if basic hygiene and service standards are missing.

TikTalk Café is located in a prime and high-footfall area like Anna Nagar. Customers naturally expect better standards.

Good food alone is not sufficient—cleanliness, hygiene, and basic maintenance are equally important for customers to enjoy their meal confidently.
